newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S'pore oil products see gas oil firm despite India.
newsitem.headline: S'pore oil products see gas oil firm despite India.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices were steady to firm on Monday despite earlier predictions of a free-fall on news that India bought only 120,000 tonnes of gas oil in its tender for October delivery, traders said.

Some traders said compared with Europe and the MidEast, Asian prices were low. However, other traders said soft regional demand and ample supplies did not justify current strong prices especially after India bought small volumes two months in a row. Traders widely expect China to support the market when prices started to dip and there was even talk that China bought two prompt cargoes at $199-$199.50 a tonne c+f on Friday.

But other traders said current levels remained high for China who was not in a hurry to buy, especially as stocks were high in Hong Kong, available supplies from north China and from S. Korea. China was still holding out at $192-$195 a tonne c+f. India's small imports would leave MidEast suppliers with excess cargoes, especially one percent grade which would cast a shadow on the market. Traders were already seeing MidEast premiums dipping to 25 from 70 cents. Singapore paper September gas oil rose 10 cents to $25.45/$25.60 with a deal at $25.48. A bid and offer for 200,000 barrels of September 20-24 gas oil was seen at $25.30, around Friday's levels.

Gasoline was largely unchanged in quiet trading. The market was reassured by Taiwan's buy tender for a 250,000-barrel 95-octane cargo for October arrival. Talks of exports from the region to Africa and the west was not confirmed. Taiwan also issued a tender to buy a 30,000 tonnes naphtha cargo for October delivery. Naphtha edged down slightly on lower crude values with a September paper deal done at $19.80 and October traded at $19.65. Fuel oil was steady with the market seeking directions due to IPE's close. Traders said physical fundamentals were balanced. While supplies were limited, demand from China, India and Thailand were also thin. --SINGAPORE NEWSROOM (+65-8703084)
